title: Onboarding to Impact: Cross-Functional Playbook and Tooling Checklist
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose

This playbook prescribes a repeatable, measurable onboarding-to-impact program for cross-functional hires at Redwood Inference (engineering, product, SRE, sales engineering). It integrates: role-specific ramp milestones, benefits orientation checkpoints, a compact internal tools setup guide, and a mentorship/managering cadence to accelerate new hire contribution while preserving consistent evaluator signals for career ladder placement.

Scope

- New hires in engineering, product, SRE, and go-to-market who start on or after 2026-01-01.
- Contractors on engagements longer than 90 days.
- Companion to the New Hire Orientation and Tooling Guide — this doc focuses on ramp metrics, role mapping to ladders, and impact-oriented checklists.

Principles

1. Ship small impact early: identify a 1–2 week task that yields measurable product or infra impact.
2. Consistent signals: use the same set of ramp checkpoints for equivalent IC levels across teams.
3. Reduce cognitive overhead: centralize tooling steps and account requests in a single preboarding checklist.
4. Growth through mentorship: every hire has a manager and a cross-team buddy for 90 days.

Roles & Ramp Milestones (summary)

- IC1 / Associate (entry): ramp target 30 days for basic tooling, 90 days for independent execution on scoped tickets.
- IC2 / Mid: ramp target 14 days for primary services, 60 days to own a small component and own-oncall shift.
- IC3 / Senior: ramp target 7 days for infra orientation, 30 days to lead a small cross-team initiative.
- Staff/Principal: custom plan with 90/180/360 checkpoints; expect observable cross-team influence by 180 days.

For each hire, the manager assigns a primary "first-impact" ticket with acceptance criteria and metrics (throughput, latency, UX flow completion, bug count reduced, etc.).

Onboarding Phases & Checklist (Owner indicated)

1) Preboarding (People Ops) — before day 0
- Create HR packet and send welcome email with start-of-day schedule, team launch link, and hardware plan.
- Provision SSO invite (Okta) and request accounts: GitHub org, GCP/AWS console access, Slack, Jira, Confluence.
- Hardware ship (if applicable): target ship date = start_date - 7 days.
- Invite to #team-{team-name} and #welcome channel.

2) Week 0–1: Foundation (Manager / Buddy)
- Day 0: orientation session (People Ops) — benefits overview, payroll, PTO/RTO policy, security baseline.
- Day 1: team kickoff, meet manager & buddy, assign first-impact ticket.
- Tooling sprint: complete CLI login, environment bootstrap, repo access, and local dev run.
  - Example CLI snippet (internal):
    - rwd-login --team <team> # obtains short-lived credentials
    - gcloud auth login --brief # cloud console access
- 3 mandatory read items: infra-standards, code-of-conduct, oncall runbook for the team.

3) Month 1: Contribution & Feedback (Manager / Mentor)
- Deliver first-impact ticket with acceptance tests.
- Weekly 1:1s documented in Confluence with outcomes and blockers.
- 30-day review: manager completes the Ramp Checklist and rates progress (On Track / Needs Support / Off Track).

4) Month 2–3: Ownership & Evaluation (Manager / People Ops)
- 60-day objective: own a recurring task (monitoring dashboard, test ownership, or feature area).
- 90-day milestone meeting: manager + peer reviewers confirm readiness for role-level expectations and map to career ladder step.

Mentorship & Managering Model

- Each hire is assigned: manager (primary owner), buddy (peer-level, cross-team), and a mentor (optional senior IC for career conversations).
- Cadence: 1:1 weekly (manager), weekly buddy sync for first 30 days, mentor check-ins biweekly for first 90 days.
- Mentorship topics: product context, architecture overview, career ladder calibration, and networking.

Benefits Orientation (People Ops owner)

- New hire session covers: health plans, flexible returnship and sabbatical basics, parental leave, commuter stipend, and our Employee Assistance Program.
- Benefits checklist to complete in first 14 days: enroll in medical, confirm 401(k) elections, add emergency contact, and set up payroll deposit.

Internal Tools Quickstart (Engineering DEX & Infra)

- Required accounts and initial access (order matters):
  1) Okta / SSO
  2) Slack (#team channels, #eng-all)
  3) GitHub team membership + repo write access
  4) Cloud console (GCP or AWS) with IAM role 'dev:standard'
  5) Confluence and Jira access
  6) Redwood Console demo tenancy (read-only)

- Common troubleshooting commands:
  - rwd-login --help
  - scripts/bootstrap-local.sh --fast
  - ./tools/check-permissions.sh --expected dev:standard

- Safety net: if repo or cloud access is missing after 48 hours, raise a ticket to #it-ops with tag @it-ops-escalation.

Ramp Success Metrics (what "on track" looks like)

- Technical ICs: successful merge of a non-trivial PR with passing CI, ability to run a component end-to-end locally, successful oncall handoff.
- Product / PM / Design: delivered scoped discovery notes, aligned roadmap piece, stakeholder demo.
- SRE / Infra: owned a deploy, updated runbook, met a latency or error reduction target.

Evaluation & Career Ladder Mapping

- At 90 days the manager proposes a ladder placement signal packet with: key deliverables, peer feedback (2–3 reviewers), and a self-assessment. People Ops stores the packet in the new-hire file.
- Promotion & leveling exceptions are processed via the standard role-framework flow; use the Role Calibration rubric from /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/role-framework-and-growth-paths-2025.json.

Templates & Artifacts (copyable)

- First-Impact Ticket Template:
  - Title: [team] first-impact — short description
  - Acceptance: measurable metric, supporting tests, rollout plan
  - Owner: new hire

- 30/60/90 Review Template (to be completed in Confluence)
  - Objectives, accomplishments, blockers, development goals, manager rating.

Escalation & Exceptions

- If a new hire is Off Track after 30 days: manager must file a New Hire Support Plan (NHSP) and notify People Ops within 48 hours.
- Hardware or account delays > 3 business days: People Ops escalates to IT and report to the hiring manager.

Ownership & Contacts

- People Ops: Maya Chen (onboarding program owner) — people-ops@redwood.ai
- Engineering DEX: Daniel Park — dex@redwood.ai
- Infrastructure & Security: Aisha Rahman — infra-security@redwood.ai

Appendix A — Example 90-day Ramp Checklist (table)

| Checkpoint | Who | Expected by | Success signal |
|-----------|-----|------------|----------------|
| SSO & Slack | IT/People Ops | Day 0 | Logged into Slack and joined #team channel |
| Local dev run | Buddy/Engineer | Week 1 | Ran component locally and executed tests |
| First-impact merge | Manager | Day 30 | Merged PR + green CI + acceptance tests |
| Oncall shadow | Team oncall | Day 60 | Completed shadow shift without critical incidents |
| Career ladder packet | Manager + Peers | Day 90 | Packet submitted and reviewed by People Ops |

Notes

This document is deliberately pragmatic: keep the "first-impact" concept small and measurable. Managers: ensure clarity in acceptance criteria — ambiguous tickets slow ramp. People Ops: maintain the tooling onboarding checklist and the account provisioning SLA (target 72 hours).
